title: Arc length and central angle as a fraction of the circle
subtitle: Circles · 10 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **10 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 2 Easy, 2 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question mentions an arc, a central angle, a circumference, or a radius or diameter.
- It asks for an arc length, an angle, the circumference, or what fraction of the circle an arc is.
- The angle may be in degrees or in radians.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Set up one proportion: arc length ÷ circumference = central angle ÷ 360° (or ÷ 2π in radians).
- 2) Fill in the two or three values you know and solve for the missing one.
- Remember that the degree measure of an arc equals its central angle.
- 3) Use d = 2r and C = 2πr = πd to move between radius, diameter and circumference.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Not useful beyond working out the arithmetic.
There is nothing to graph, so the whole task is spotting the proportion.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You mix up the arc's measure in degrees with its length.
Or you divide by 180 instead of 360.
Or you use the diameter where the formula needs the radius, which is off by a factor of 2.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You mix up the arc's measure in degrees with its length.
Or you divide by 180 instead of 360.
